findings.summary: Registering a scene must LOWER TODO.md, and this diff left it saying the opposite in three places: the unregistered count read 93 where it is now 87, the runtime-sweep gate still listed 16, 43 and 204 (and 129 in its removeFromScene twin) as scenes that do not compile, and the integrate-first list still named 16, 43, 129 and 270 -- all registered -- while claiming 59 scenes for a list that expanded to 57. Counts recomputed from the registry and the corpus rather than adjusted by hand.

The golden and the status preview were untracked. Committing without them would have shipped a manifest referenceSha256 pointing at a file no clone has, failing corpus-scenes.test.ts for everyone else.

The status row dated the capability to the scene that shipped it ("the spelling the browser erasure folds since scene 43"). No other row in the table carries provenance, and the load-bearing half survives the trim; the reasoning already lives in the registry comment, which is where neighbouring entries keep it.

Verified rather than assumed, since a registration is all recorded facts: all four digests recomputed and matched, the entry's position checked against each of the five enumerations that order scenes, the thresholds checked against the measured reports (0 full and region on both backends, byte-identical between them), and the background colour sampled from the golden -- it genuinely rounds to 51,51,76 where 30 other entries use 77, so the value is measured, not copied.

Confirmed the bare arm is the only registrable one: enableThinInstanceGpuCulling appears nowhere in src/, so the ?culling arm would refuse at generation, and the generated main.cpp carries no culling reference at all -- the erasure folds the condition away.
